aerodynamics.name: Aerodynamics

front_wing.name: Front Wing (FW)
front_wing.description: Controls the downforce at the front of the car. Higher values create more downforce, increasing front-end grip and reducing understeer. Lower values reduce drag but may cause understeer in corners.
front_wing.increase_effect: More front grip, less understeer, slightly more drag, better turn-in
front_wing.decrease_effect: Less front grip, more understeer, less drag, higher top speed

rear_wing.name: Rear Wing (RW)
rear_wing.description: Controls the downforce at the rear of the car. Higher values increase rear stability and traction out of corners but add drag. Lower values reduce drag for higher speeds but can cause oversteer.
rear_wing.increase_effect: More rear stability, less oversteer, better traction, more drag
rear_wing.decrease_effect: Less rear grip, more oversteer, less drag, higher top speed

aerodynamics.general_advice: Aerodynamics is the primary balance tool. High-downforce tracks (Monaco, Hungary, Singapore) need high wings (35-45). Low-downforce tracks (Monza, Spa) need low wings (10-20). Use FW/RW ratio to balance understeer and oversteer.

transmission.name: Transmission

differential_on_throttle.name: Differential On Throttle (Diff On)
differential_on_throttle.description: Controls how much the rear wheels lock together when accelerating. Higher values improve traction out of corners but can cause understeer. Lower values allow more rotation but may cause wheelspin.
differential_on_throttle.increase_effect: Better traction, less wheelspin, more mid-corner understeer
differential_on_throttle.decrease_effect: More rotation, easier to turn, possible wheelspin, potential oversteer

differential_off_throttle.name: Differential Off Throttle (Diff Off)
differential_off_throttle.description: Controls rear wheel locking when coasting or braking. Higher values stabilize the car but reduce turn-in. Lower values improve rotation and corner entry.
differential_off_throttle.increase_effect: More stable under braking, less rotation, understeer on entry
differential_off_throttle.decrease_effect: Better turn-in, more rotation, potential instability under braking

transmission.general_advice: Differential controls corner exit traction and entry rotation. Tight tracks benefit from lower diff settings for rotation. Fast tracks need higher settings for stability.

suspension.name: Suspension

front_suspension.name: Front Suspension (FS)
front_suspension.description: Controls front spring stiffness. Lower values (softer) provide more mechanical grip over bumps. Higher values (stiffer) improve responsiveness on smooth tracks.
front_suspension.increase_effect: Stiffer front, less grip over bumps, more responsive, understeer
front_suspension.decrease_effect: Softer front, more grip over bumps, less responsive, less understeer

rear_suspension.name: Rear Suspension (RS)
rear_suspension.description: Controls rear spring stiffness. Softer provides traction, stiffer improves responsiveness.
rear_suspension.increase_effect: Stiffer rear, less traction over bumps, more responsive, oversteer
rear_suspension.decrease_effect: Softer rear, more traction, better exit grip, less oversteer

front_anti_roll_bar.name: Front Anti-Roll Bar (FARB)
front_anti_roll_bar.description: Controls body roll at the front during cornering. Higher values reduce roll and increase responsiveness but can reduce grip.
front_anti_roll_bar.increase_effect: Less body roll, more responsive, potential understeer
front_anti_roll_bar.decrease_effect: More mechanical grip, softer turn-in, less understeer

rear_anti_roll_bar.name: Rear Anti-Roll Bar (RARB)
rear_anti_roll_bar.description: Controls body roll at the rear during cornering.
rear_anti_roll_bar.increase_effect: Less body roll, more responsive, potential oversteer
rear_anti_roll_bar.decrease_effect: More mechanical grip, better traction, less oversteer

front_ride_height.name: Front Ride Height (FRH)
front_ride_height.description: Distance between front of car and ground. Lower increases downforce but risks bottoming out.
front_ride_height.increase_effect: Less downforce, higher ride, safer over bumps, understeer
front_ride_height.decrease_effect: More downforce, better aero efficiency, risk of bottoming

rear_ride_height.name: Rear Ride Height (RRH)
rear_ride_height.description: Distance between rear of car and ground.
rear_ride_height.increase_effect: Less downforce, higher ride, safer over bumps, oversteer
rear_ride_height.decrease_effect: More downforce, better traction, risk of bottoming

suspension.general_advice: Suspension controls mechanical grip and ride comfort. Bumpy tracks (Singapore, Baku, Monaco) need softer suspension. Smooth tracks (Bahrain, Abu Dhabi) can use stiffer settings.

suspension_geometry.name: Suspension Geometry

front_camber.name: Front Camber (FC)
front_camber.description: Angle of front wheels. Negative camber (tilted inward at top) improves cornering grip but reduces straight-line grip.
front_camber.increase_effect: More negative camber, better cornering grip, worse straight-line
front_camber.decrease_effect: Less negative camber, better acceleration/braking, worse cornering

rear_camber.name: Rear Camber (RC)
rear_camber.increase_effect: More negative camber, better cornering grip, traction loss
rear_camber.decrease_effect: Less negative camber, better traction out of corners

front_toe.name: Front Toe (FTO)
front_toe.description: Angle of front wheels viewed from above. Positive (toe-in) stabilizes, negative (toe-out) improves turn-in.
front_toe.increase_effect: More toe-in, stable at high speed, understeer, tire wear

rear_toe.name: Rear Toe In (RTI)
rear_toe.increase_effect: More stable, less oversteer, tire wear

suspension_geometry.general_advice: Geometry fine-tunes handling characteristics. More negative camber for twisty tracks. Neutral settings for high-speed circuits. Geometry changes are small but impactful.

brakes.name: Brakes

brake_bias.name: Brake Bias
brake_bias.description: Distribution of braking force between front and rear. Higher values send more force to front wheels.
brake_bias.increase_effect: More front braking, stable but potential understeer
brake_bias.decrease_effect: More rear braking, rotation but potential instability

brake_pressure.name: Brake Pressure
brake_pressure.description: Overall braking force. Higher values give more initial bite.
brake_pressure.increase_effect: Stronger braking, shorter distances, lockup risk

brakes.general_advice: Brakes affect corner entry. High-braking tracks (Montreal, Baku) may need higher pressure. Brake bias around 56-60% is typical. Adjust based on lockup tendencies.

tyres.name: Tyre Pressures

front_right_pressure.name: Front Right Tyre Pressure (FRT)
front_right_pressure.description: Pressure in front right tyre. Affects grip, temperature, and wear.
front_right_pressure.increase_effect: Less grip, cooler temps, less wear, overheating protection
front_right_pressure.decrease_effect: More grip, hotter temps, more wear, better feel

front_left_pressure.name: Front Left Tyre Pressure (FLT)
front_left_pressure.increase_effect: Less grip, cooler temps, less wear
front_left_pressure.decrease_effect: More grip, hotter temps, more wear

rear_right_pressure.name: Rear Right Tyre Pressure (RRT)
rear_right_pressure.increase_effect: Less traction, cooler temps, less wear
rear_right_pressure.decrease_effect: More traction, hotter temps, more wear

rear_left_pressure.name: Rear Left Tyre Pressure (RLT)
rear_left_pressure.increase_effect: Less traction, cooler temps, less wear
rear_left_pressure.decrease_effect: More traction, hotter temps, more wear

tyres.general_advice: Tyre pressures balance grip vs temperature management. Lower pressures give more grip but risk overheating. Higher pressures protect from overheating but reduce grip. Hot tracks or high tyre wear tracks need higher pressures. Start with baseline (23-25 front, 21-23 rear) and adjust based on telemetry.
